A new game. You play White, so your opponent moves first, right after you choose it.

Rules: Chinese area scoring, with 7 points of komi for White; a level score is a draw. Simple ko: an immediate recapture is refused, and the board marks the ko point when there is one. Suicide is not allowed. An invalid move is refused with the rule it broke, and the turn stays with you. The game ends after two passes in a row or a resignation; a game that reaches 243 moves is scored where it stands. After two passes the engine scores the position as it stands and decides itself which stones are dead.

## Opponents

Your opponent is KataGo playing in the style of a human of the rank you choose. The ladder, weakest to strongest: 20k, 18k, 16k, 14k, 12k, 10k, 8k, 6k, 4k, 2k, 1d, 3d, 5d, 7d, 9d. I lost game 194, playing White against the 12k opponent: I resigned at move 58 (B+R).

**What happened:**
- **Opening went well.** Black opened at tengen and built a wall down the E column (E3/E5/E7). I built a solid wall down the G column on the right, worth about 28 points. Around move 40, count.py had me roughly 10 points ahead.
- **The left group died.** Black had taken both left corners (C3/B2 below, B7/B8 above), and D5 later closed the centre side, which left my left group with eye space only at A3–A6 plus B5. While I played 1–2 point edge moves (F7, H1, F9, G9, H2), Black played inside it: A5, A3, then B1, C2 and A1. The A3 eye ended up depending on my lone A2 stone, and A1 made it false. With one eye, the 12-stone group was dead. That left me about 35 points with komi against 53, so I resigned.
- **The mistake** was the same one already in the notes many times: I never counted that group's eyes once it was walled in on three sides. Around moves 36–40 it needed A3/A2 shape or D5 before any boundary move.
